messages.content: Write a customer case study about a company that adopted a continuous delivery platform and now deploys more often. Around 250 words.

The customer is made up. You didn't name one, so read every number as a placeholder.

**Northwind Cargo: from a release every six weeks to 45 a week**

Northwind Cargo hauls freight for roughly 400 regional shippers. Through 2025, its 32 engineers shipped on a six-week train. On the Thursday that came due, four of them stayed past dinner, worked down a 140-step checklist by hand, and waited to find out whether any of the ~300 commits in the batch had broken checkout.

"Batch size was the whole problem," says Priya Raman, head of platform engineering. "A failure told us nothing. Which of the 300? We'd burn two days bisecting."

The platform went in that January. The first quarter was dull work: containerize two legacy services, turn the checklist wiki page into migration steps that actually ran, and get the test suite under 11 minutes so it could run on every pull request.

Then the cadence broke open. Merges land on main behind feature flags and deploy on merge, about 45 times a week. Rollbacks haven't disappeared, twice a month give or take, but one takes 90 seconds instead of a night.

By month eight: change failure rate down from 18% to 4%. Merge-to-production median down from 31 days to 26 minutes. On-call no longer plans around release Thursday, since there isn't one.

Raman won't overclaim. "The tool didn't fix our tests. We fixed our tests, and then the tool earned its place. Ship broken code faster and you get broken code, faster."

Swap in a real company, real quotes, real DORA numbers, and the shape holds.
